# Grace & John Ashdown

IDA INTERVENES P86](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0086), [v5 CHAPTER XX. GRACE MAKES A FRIEND P4](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0004), +3 more</sub>

## Shared scenes

> Mary discusses her fear of damnation and beatings with [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) and [Grace](../character/grace.md) before being introduced to the [Carrows](../codex/factions.md#carrows) at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). Afterwards, the girls arrange for Mary to sleep in the parsonage garret room. Later that night, [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) comforts Mary in the garret, where Mary expresses her fears and jealousy before they reconcile and fall asleep.
>

> Mary and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) converse about faith and the possibility of Mr. Ashdown remarrying, which leaves [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) frightened and tearful. Meanwhile, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reads through the night and contemplates his late wife, oblivious to Ida's distress.
>

> During a church service, [Grace](../character/grace.md) interrupts the collection to publicly defend her father and clarify the misunderstanding behind their Sunday cleaning. The next day, she and Edmund ride pigs down Main Street, drawing mixed reactions from townspeople and the local doctor's family. Later, Miss Winifred visits [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) at [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) to complain about Grace's antics, but [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) defends the child's brave intentions.
>

> [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) becomes engrossed in [German](../codex/factions.md#german) theology, neglecting his duties and family. Mrs. Hector Twiss visits the manse and proposes adopting [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), but Ashdown firmly rejects her offer. Outraged, Mrs. [Twiss](../character/twiss.md) criticizes his parenting before departing, leaving Ashdown deeply shaken and introspective.
>

> Mrs. [Twiss](../character/twiss.md) leaves the manse after scolding the children and Mr. Ashdown. Disturbed by her accusations about his parenting, Mr. Ashdown reflects on his children's needs and decides to seek company and comfort by visiting [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) and [Harriet Ainslie](../character/harriet-ainslie.md).
>

> Edmund finishes his fight with [Dan Coyle](../character/coyle.md), forcing Dan to retract his insults. On his way home through [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), Edmund encounters Mr. Ashdown, who praises him for defending the honor of women. Later, after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) tends to Edmund's bruises, Miss Winifred and [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) discuss the fight as well as rumors regarding Mr. Ashdown courting [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md).
>

> After being teased at school about the loss of her rooster [Adam](../character/adam.md), [Grace](../character/grace.md) goes toward [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) seeking comfort from Mrs. [Carrow](../character/carrow.md). In [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), she meets [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md), who listens sympathetically to Grace's grief and offers her a pet canary. [Grace](../character/grace.md) returns home feeling comforted and tells her father and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) how much she loves [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md).
>

> [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) walks through [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) on his way to propose to [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md), reflecting on his feelings for her and his reluctance to take a "suitable" second wife. Meanwhile, [Harriet Ainslie](../character/harriet-ainslie.md) prepares to hold [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to a past vow to reject him despite their fond mutual regard, leaving [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) anxious about turning him down.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P0](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P1](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)_

> The [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes [Ida Ashdown](../character/ida-ashdown.md) to faint during the church service. Doctor [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading [Grace](../character/grace.md) to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) before returning to his theological studies.
>

> [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) gossip-shares village rumors with [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) about why [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) refused their father's proposal and how [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) threw an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy. Learning of the incident, Mr. Ashdown intends to whip [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) in his study, but relents at the last second when he sees his late wife's eyes in the boy, leaving both father and son deeply shaken.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXXIII. RUPERT IS—NOT—WHIPPED
